- name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          name: coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2

      # junit durations for the weekly shard-rebalance.yml (retention 7d so
      # a quiet week never starves it into the file-count fallback).

      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          name: coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2

      # junit durations for the weekly shard-rebalance.yml (retention 7d so
      # a quiet week never starves it into the file-count fallback).

blocks.text:
- name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          name: coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2

      # junit durations for the weekly shard-rebalance.yml (retention 7d so
      # a quiet week never starves it into the file-count fallback).

# Rework: red `CRAP + duplication` guard fixed (Quality gate aggregate falls with it)

CI on the previous rework head (`ddadc557`) failed exactly two checks: **CRAP + duplication** (the `guards` job) and **Quality gate** (the aggregate — its only red input is `guards`). One root cause, fixed below. No review threads carried code findings this round (all three from the previous round were resolved; the 7 open conversations in `pr_discussions_raw.json` all have `threadId: null` / `rootCommentId: null` — top-level status posts, review-verdict records marked "do not edit or reply", and fleet monitor notes — so `outputs/review_replies.json` is an empty reply set).

## Issues/Notes

- 🚨 **CRAP ratchet breach** — `dart pub global run crap4dart analyze` on the failing head: `Max CRAP: 12.0008 — FAIL (threshold: 12.0)`. The sole offender above the ratchet: `ModelRolesResolver._buildEntry` (`lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart:206`) measured **CC 12 at 56/57 lines (98.25 %)** → CRAP = 144·(1−cov)³ + 12 = **12.00078 > 12.0** (strict-greater gate). Everything else sat at exactly 12.0 (the tolerated CC-3@0% / CC-12@100% tiers) and passed.
- The uncovered line is the smol-takeover closure's `on ConfigException` clause inside `_buildEntry`'s `buildTakeover` — **uncoverable by tests in place**: the VM's coverage instrumentation never credits a catch-clause line even when the handler runs (also independently established by the merged-in parallel fix `b8d049890`). The method had been riding the exactly-12.0 edge; any net growth tipped it.
- Reproduced locally before touching code (the CI job logs are not readable with the available token — 404): full CI-shaped coverage reproduction (4 shards + the jsr trio via `scripts/test_shards.json` targets, `coverage:format_coverage`, same commands as the `test-core`/`guards` jobs) → same `12.0008 > 12.0` FAIL. The remaining hard-fail steps of `guards` were verified green on the failing head first (loc scope: 883 files PASS; jscpd `lib/`: 0.77 % < 1.0 % PASS; cross-module dupx: PASS) — isolating the ratchet as the only red.

## Approach

Two stacked extractions, both behavior-preserving, landing on the merged tree (a parallel lane's `b8d049890` — the smol-takeover split — arrived mid-rework and was merged by the harness; this lane's change is layered on top):

1. **`_registryLeg` extraction (this lane's fix)** — the issue #1552 registry leg (catalog miss → `customProviders:` name match → apiType spec → `_throughCustomEntry` defaults → unknown-provider / unknown-adapter-dialect skips) moves out of `_buildEntry` into a `(ModelRef, ProviderSpec)? _registryLeg(...)` helper that owns the whole gh-760 skip+degrade contract for the leg: null return = skip already reported and classified, the caller just degrades. **CC 12 → 11**, which is ratchet-proof at any coverage (CC-11 @ 98 %+ ≈ 11.0007 < 12.0). First cut kept the generic skip in the caller and the UT-3 regression test caught the doubled skip reason immediately (dialect + unknown-provider both reported) — reshaped so the leg owns both null paths; suite green after.
2. **`_smolTakeoverStream` extraction (merged from `b8d049890`, kept)** — the uncoverable catch-clause leaves `_buildEntry`'s span entirely; its new IT pins the null-takeover contract.

Net: no behavior change (gh-760 degrade contract, skip wording, and the #1552 resolution order byte-identical — the UT-1/UT-2/UT-3/REG-2 and boot-IT suites prove it), CC down, the uncoverable line gone from the measured method.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart` — `_registryLeg` helper (+ the call site now degrades via `(ref, spec) = viaRegistry` record assignment); `_smolTakeoverStream` helper (merged from the parallel lane).
- `test/model_roles/silent_stream_policy_wiring_test.dart` — parallel lane's null-takeover IT (merged; passing).
- No test changes needed for the CRAP fix itself: the ratchet gate is the regression test for it (RED: `12.0008 > 12.0` reproduced on the failing head before the refactor; GREEN: re-measured after — see Test Coverage).

## Test Coverage

- **CRAP ratchet (the failing gate)**: re-run on the fixed tree over a fresh CI-shaped full-suite coverage reproduction (`dart test --coverage` shards 0–3 + jsr trio, `format_coverage`, `crap4dart analyze`): max CRAP back **≤ 12.0 — PASS** (numbers below from the final run).

- **Behavior**: `test/model_roles/` + `test/cli/roles_custom_providers_boot_test.dart` + `test/cli/startup_test.dart` — **421 passed** (all UT-1/UT-2/UT-3/REG-2 layouts, the boot ITs, the AC4 notice-stream IT, and the parallel lane's null-takeover IT); `dart analyze` clean; `dart format --set-exit-if-changed` clean on all PR-touched Dart files.
- Core-shard full runs on the fixed tree: **shard 2800+2614+2415+3124 tests passed** (10 environmental skips), jsr trio 45 passed — mirrors the CI `test-core` shape the guards consume.

- 🚨 **CRAP ratchet breach** — `dart pub global run crap4dart analyze` on the failing head: `Max CRAP: 12.0008 — FAIL (threshold: 12.0)`. Everything else sat at exactly 12.0 (the tolerated CC-3@0% / CC-12@100% tiers) and passed.
- The uncovered line is the smol-takeover closure's `on ConfigException` clause inside `_buildEntry`'s `buildTakeover` — **uncoverable by tests in place**: the VM's coverage instrumentation never credits a catch-clause line even when the handler runs (also independently established by the merged-in parallel fix `b8d049890`). The method had been riding the exactly-12.0 edge; any net growth tipped it.

## Approach

Two stacked extractions, both behavior-preserving, landing on the merged tree (a parallel lane's `b8d049890` — the smol-takeover split — arrived mid-rework and was merged by the harness; this lane's change is layered on top):

1. **`_registryLeg` extraction (this lane's fix)** — the issue #1552 registry leg (catalog miss → `customProviders:` name match → apiType spec → `_throughCustomEntry` defaults → unknown-provider / unknown-adapter-dialect skips) moves out of `_buildEntry` into a `(ModelRef, ProviderSpec)? _registryLeg(...)` helper that owns the whole gh-760 skip+degrade contract for the leg: null return = skip already reported and classified, the caller just degrades. **CC 12 → 11**, which is ratchet-proof at any coverage (CC-11 @ 98 %+ ≈ 11.0007 < 12.0). First cut kept the generic skip in the caller and the UT-3 regression test caught the doubled skip reason immediately (dialect + unknown-provider both reported) — reshaped so the leg owns both null paths; suite green after.
2. **`_smolTakeoverStream` extraction (merged from `b8d049890`, kept)** — the uncoverable catch-clause leaves `_buildEntry`'s span entirely; its new IT pins the null-takeover contract.

- 🚨 **CRAP ratchet breach** — `dart pub global run crap4dart analyze` on the failing head: `Max CRAP: 12.0008 — FAIL (threshold: 12.0)`. Everything else sat at exactly 12.0 (the tolerated CC-3@0% / CC-12@100% tiers) and passed.
- The uncovered line is the smol-takeover closure's `on ConfigException` clause inside `_buildEntry`'s `buildTakeover` — **uncoverable by tests in place**: the VM's coverage instrumentation never credits a catch-clause line even when the handler runs (also independently established by the merged-in parallel fix `b8d049890`). The method had been riding the exactly-12.0 edge; any net growth tipped it.
- Reproduced locally before touching code (the CI job logs are not readable with the available token — 404): full CI-shaped coverage reproduction (4 shards + the jsr trio via `scripts/test_shards.json` targets, `coverage:format_coverage`, same commands as the `test-core`/`guards` jobs) → same `12.0008 > 12.0` FAIL. Two stacked extractions, both behavior-preserving, landing on the merged tree (a parallel lane's `b8d049890` — the smol-takeover split — arrived mid-rework and was merged by the harness; this lane's change is layered on top):

First cut kept the generic skip in the caller and the UT-3 regression test caught the doubled skip reason immediately (dialect + unknown-provider both reported) — reshaped so the leg owns both null paths; suite green after.
